title: Choose the visual world for Signal Scout
question: The roll assigned Herbarium Accession. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each sketch shows the live run view (the screen interviewers watch).

options.label: Herbarium Accession
options.lineage: herbarium specimen sheets, collection labels and determination slips
options.thesis: Every finding is a collected specimen with its collection label; nothing reaches a draft until a determination slip says verified.
options.viewport: Botanical-green nav rail; a pipeline accession ledger on the left; the selected hook mounted centre with its collection label (source, collected date, accession S3·G1) and a pinned 'det. verified' slip; the draft on the right.
options.risk: The botanical metaphor turns whimsical if it leaks past type, palette, density and the slip; it must stay a working tool.

raised.raise: Findings and labels snap to a visible 12-column cell grid, so evidence reads as a catalogue, not a feed.
Dashboard rows carry twice the information density: status, hook, evidence count, sources and active time.
A run whose status changes moves in place and holds its state colour until you've seen it.

options.label: The Fact-Checker's Proof
options.thesis: The draft is a galley proof: every claim highlighted and keyed to a source in the margin, rejections struck in red pencil.
options.viewport: The draft as a marked-up proof with margin source callouts; pipeline as a checklist above it.
options.risk: Familiar: it's the closest to the current build and to the editorial look most runs in this category land on.

options.label: Centre-Rail Reference
options.thesis: Draft and evidence twinned around a rail of source keys; every sentence is keyed to the quote that licenses it.
options.viewport: Draft column and evidence column twinned around a vermilion key rail (S1, S3…), apparatus in the margin.
options.case: Fuses strongly with the mechanism (claim to quote); loses audience identification, since reps don't read scholarly editions.
options.risk: Reads academic and slow on a live demo.

options.label: Midnight Transit Line
options.thesis: The pipeline is a transit line: stages are stations, clarification is an interchange loop, 'not enough signal' is a terminus.
options.viewport: Midnight-blue header band carrying the live line diagram across the top; evidence and draft panels below on a light ground.
options.case: Holds audience identification: interviewers grasp the live process instantly. Loses product clarity on evidence, where the map can't show quotes.
options.risk: The map can upstage the evidence and draft, which are the actual product.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.case: Fuses poorly: departures don't map to evidence; the pass metaphor adds nothing to verification.
options.kept: A changed row moves in place and stays lit until noticed.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.case: Fuses poorly: monumental letterforms fight a dense working screen.
options.kept: A visible construction grid as real structure.

options.label: Japanese High-Density
options.case: Fuses poorly: density without a story; the demo needs one clear focus.
options.kept: Density courage on the run list.

options.label: Split-Flap Concourse
options.case: Fuses poorly: an instrument costume on a working screen.
options.kept: State changes restyle a row without breaking the grid.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern SaaS workspace (Linear / Attio register), executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, run header, three tidy panels: pipeline, evidence, draft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any other AI tool demo.
